Currently enrolled, or recently graduated with a degree in computer science, software engineering, or a related engineering field is required, or equivalent demonstrated by significant hands-on experience with multiple programming languages.   • AppSec Tool Management

    • Participate in client-facing tool discussions and shadowed engagements under mentorship

A lot of this is normalization, deduplication, and edge case handling.

  • Integrate AI into real-world workflows. Put LLMs and ML models into production for real workflows: RAG pipelines, embeddings, prompt execution, agentic systems, fine-tuned models. Production means reliable, monitored, and cost-conscious.

  • Design systems that scale. Build systems that will hold up as we grow 10x, while being practical about what to invest in now vs. what can wait.

  • Develop performant APIs and services. Create robust interfaces and internal services that power our product end-to-end, ensuring reliability, security, and a seamless experience for customers.

  • Collaborate closely with users. Join customer calls, hear what's working and what isn't, and build in response. Rapidly iterate to deliver solutions that genuinely move the needle for comms/public affairs teams.

  • Shape Clipbook's engineering culture. As one of the first engineers, you'll influence everything — code quality, system design principles, documentation standards, and how we build as a team. We believe leaders stay hands-on: even as we grow, everyone (including managers) continues to ship.

What We're Looking For

  • 2–10+ years building and scaling production backend systems. You've taken systems from zero to production and owned the full lifecycle. Strong across backend fundamentals (services, data models, distributed systems), with deeper expertise in one or more areas — and a desire to keep expanding your breadth over time.

  • Genuine excitement to build quickly & ship fast. We care about getting things into users' hands and iterating from there.

  • You take ownership. When something is broken or unclear, you fix it or flag it without waiting to be asked.

  • Comfortable with ambiguity. You make reasonable calls with incomplete information, communicate them clearly, and adjust as you learn more.

  • Strong experience with cloud infrastructure, containerization, and CI/CD. We're building systems that will one day serve Fortune 500 executives in real-time — so reliability matters. Familiarity with AWS/GCP, containerization (Docker/K8s), and CI/CD pipelines ensures we can deliver high uptime and iterate quickly.

  • A future leader. You'll help shape our engineering culture and can quickly grow into leadership as the company scales.

Technical Areas Where Depth Matters (one or more)

  • Data Engineering: Spark, Kafka, Flink, BigQuery, streaming pipelines, ETL at scale.

  • Distributed Systems: High-volume scaling, fault tolerance, eventual consistency.

  • AI/ML: LLMs in production, RAG, embeddings, fine-tuning, inference optimization.

  • Backend: Python, Node.js, PostgreSQL, high-concurrency systems.

Nice-to-Haves

  • LLM fine-tuning, RLHF, or eval pipelines.

  • Web scraping and API integrations at scale.

  • Startup founder or early-stage experience is a huge plus.

What This Role Is Not

We're hiring for the application and data layer. This probably isn't the right fit if your background is primarily in firmware, embedded systems, hardware engineering, networking, or infrastructure/DevOps.

A Few Things Worth Knowing

  • We care more about what you ship than when or where you work, but this is an early-stage company growing fast. The pace reflects that. Our culture is intense and driven by H&H (hunger and hustle).

  • As one of the first engineers, you'll wear a lot of hats. There's no platform team to hand things off to yet.

Compensation & Benefits

  • Salary: $150K–$220K

  • Equity: Early-stage grant with significant upside

  • Benefits: Medical, dental, vision, 401(k), unlimited PTO

Growth: A clear path to engineering leadership as we scale

Who We Are

Imprint helps the world's best brands grow the lifetime value of their customers. We started with co-branded credit cards and rebuilt them to be smarter, more rewarding, and brand-first. We partner with companies like Crate & Barrel, Rakuten, , H-E-B, Fetch, and Shell to launch modern credit programs that deepen loyalty, unlock savings, and drive growth. We combine advanced payments infrastructure, intelligent underwriting, and deep customer data to create delightful and personalized experiences for members as well as efficient and profitable relationships for our brand partners. Our robust technology and world-class operations allow us and our brand partners to offer powerful financial products without becoming a bank.

In the U.S., co-branded cards alone account for over $300 billion in annual spend, and most still run on decades-old legacy bank systems. Imprint is the modern alternative: flexible, embeddable, and built for how people actually pay today. Backed by Kleiner Perkins, Thrive Capital, Ribbit, and Khosla Ventures, we're building a world-class team to redefine how people pay and how brands grow. If you want to move fast, solve hard problems, and own real outcomes, we want to meet you.

About the role

Imprint's Marketing Design team builds and maintains the design systems behind a growing portfolio of partner brands — across email, web, in-app, paid, and print. Email is at the center of how we communicate with cardholders, and doing it well at scale requires both a reliable production engine and a high-quality validation layer.

We’re looking for an Email Automation & QA Specialist who thrives at the intersection of content, systems, code, and quality. You’ll be the person who:

  • Understands how emails are designed, assembled, personalized, and launched in Braze (templates, catalogs, content blocks, Liquid, localization, and tracking).

  • Builds AI automations to accelerate and standardize production.

  • Introduces an AI QA layer that flags issues early (before human review), and owns the final human QA process and quality bar.

This is a systems-and-quality role: you’ll improve and maintain our automation and QA workflows so production stays reliable as we scale.

What you’ll own

Content catalog management & template assembly (Braze)

  • Assemble new email templates from already-developed components in Braze, ensuring the final output matches the original Figma source and approved copy.

  • Build, update, and maintain reusable content blocks and catalog entries across our partner programs.

  • Manage content accuracy, localization, and versioning across a growing library of partner templates.

  • Partner with the design technologist to flag structural/component issues and improve the underlying system.

  • Build and iterate on AI-assisted workflows that convert Figma designs + copy into the content structures we use to power reusable, dynamic templates in Braze.

AI-first QA → human QA (quality pipeline)

  • Design and implement an AI QA checklist that runs before human review (e.g., link/UTM validation, Liquid variable presence, localization completeness, dark mode considerations, compliance string presence, etc.).

  • Maintain QA tooling outputs (logs, check reports, tracked issues) so QA is repeatable and measurable.

  • Conduct end-to-end human QA on every email before it reaches the lifecycle team — proofreading, link validation, rendering checks across clients and dark mode, and dynamic content verification.

  • Run inbox testing and document/resolve issues prior to deployment; continually improve the checklist based on issues found.

  • Create lightweight tools/scripts/prompts that standardize repetitive tasks and improve QA quality.

  • Own documentation, versioning, and ongoing maintenance of automations as components, partner programs, and requirements evolve.

Braze campaign & canvas support

  • Support Marketing Ops/Lifecycle with campaign and canvas builds by providing ready content catalogs and thoroughly validated templates in Braze.

  • Manage content setup, dynamic content logic, and final QA to ensure accurate and timely launches.

  • Maintain and update existing campaigns as partner programs evolve — offer swaps, compliance edits, copy updates — with automation where possible and careful review always.

Link tracking, and validation

  • Generate, manage, and QA campaign links ensuring all UTM tracking is accurate and functioning correctly.

  • Work with or similar deep linking platforms to set up and validate deep links.

  • Build automated checks to catch common tracking issues before launch (broken links, missing UTMs, wrong destinations, mismatched deep links).

Code troubleshooting & safe updates

  • Troubleshoot and make updates to HTML and Liquid code within existing email templates (within established patterns and guardrails).

  • Maintain a working knowledge of email client rendering and compatibility best practices.

  • When automation or templates hit a complexity wall, escalate appropriately — and propose systemic fixes to reduce repeats.

What we’re looking for

Essential

  • Strong systems thinking and attention to detail — you catch edge cases and take pride in error-free output.

  • Practical experience building or operating automation (AI-assisted workflows, scripts, no-code/low-code tools, or process automation) in a production environment.

  • Working knowledge of HTML and CSS for email — enough to troubleshoot, update, and QA code confidently.

  • Experience with Liquid templating or similar dynamic content systems.

  • Deep familiarity with how work moves through a production pipeline: inputs → assembly → validation → launch → iteration.

  • Comfort with tooling and operational rigor: naming conventions, documentation, change control, and ongoing maintenance.

  • Clear, proactive communication and ownership of deliverables.

Preferred

  • Experience with Braze or a comparable lifecycle marketing platform.

  • Experience with content catalog management and dynamic template logic.

  • Familiarity with UTM tracking, link management, and campaign attribution.

  • Experience with mobile deep linking platforms (e.g., ).

  • Experience with inbox testing tools and client rendering QA.

  • Experience working within a component-based design system.

How this role fits the team

This role sits within the design technology pillar of the Marketing Design team, working closely with the design technologist, content strategist, and senior designers — and partnering with Lifecycle/Marketing Ops for launches.

You’ll receive finished designs and copy, build them accurately into Braze, and hand off validated campaigns to lifecycle managers. Your lane is automation + execution quality: improving how we produce emails, ensuring the system keeps working as we scale, and maintaining a consistent quality bar across every partner send.

Description

The Director, Vendor Management is responsible for the strategic leadership and operational oversight of Indero’s Vendor Management Office (VMO) and enterprise vendor governance program. The Director establishes and maintains the vendor governance framework and oversees vendor qualification, lifecycle management, performance, risk, financial stewardship, and strategic partnerships across Indero’s vendor ecosystem. Working cross-functionally with operational teams and senior leadership, the Director ensures that vendor services support quality, compliance, scalability, cost effectiveness, and the successful delivery of clinical trials.

More specifically, the Director, Vendor Management must:

  • Adhere to and promote company organizational values and related expected behaviours, follow company standard operating procedures (SOPs) and processes, and ensure all assigned training is completed on time.
  • Own, maintain, and continuously improve Indero’s enterprise vendor governance framework, including governance tiers, oversight models, decision rights, escalation pathways, and supporting standards and tools.
  • Chair vendor governance reviews and lead Vendor Steering Committee activities, ensuring clear decisions, accountability, and follow-up on actions.
  • Develop and maintain strategic relationships with key vendors and preferred partners, establish engagement strategies, and identify opportunities for innovation, enhanced capabilities, and long-term value.
  • Establish vendor performance expectations, key performance indicators (KPIs), service level measures, and scorecards; monitor trends and report performance, risks, and improvement opportunities to relevant stakeholders.
  • Lead vendor performance remediation and continuous improvement initiatives, including root cause analysis, corrective and preventive action (CAPA) plans, and verification of action effectiveness.
  • Oversee vendor qualification, requalification, onboarding, ongoing oversight, and dequalification processes in collaboration with Quality Assurance and applicable functional teams.
  • Partner with Quality Assurance on vendor audits, compliance activities, inspection readiness, and the timely resolution of audit findings and quality issues.
  • Lead major vendor escalations, monitor systemic and enterprise-level vendor risks, and ensure material risks are communicated to senior leadership with appropriate mitigation and contingency plans.
  • Analyze vendor spend, performance, capacity, and portfolio trends to support vendor selection, sourcing strategies, resource planning, and cost optimization.
  • Contribute vendor strategy and subject matter expertise to requests for proposals, bid defence preparation, study planning, and other business development activities, as applicable.
  • Provide leadership and direction to Vendor Managers, Clinical Procurement Specialists, and other VMO resources, including workforce planning, work allocation, performance management, coaching, development, and succession planning.
  • Build vendor-management capability across the organization through guidance, training, governance forums, and effective collaboration with internal stakeholders.
  • Develop, review, and maintain vendor-management SOPs, tools, templates, processes, and training materials in alignment with applicable regulatory requirements and industry best practices.
  • Define and monitor VMO objectives, operational metrics, resource needs, and budget requirements, and implement actions to improve quality, efficiency, and scalability.
  • Employee may be assigned to other responsibilities that do not pertain to their former description, if they have the required experience, are qualified and/or have received adequate training.

Requirements

Qualifications & Experience

  • Bachelor’s degree in life sciences, business administration, supply chain, procurement, clinical research, or a related field; Master’s degree is an asset.
  • Minimum of 10 years of relevant experience in the biotechnology, pharmaceutical, and/or contract research organization (CRO) industry, including significant experience in vendor management, procurement, clinical operations, or a related function.
  • Minimum of 5 years of leadership experience, including management of direct and/or indirect reports.
  • Demonstrated experience developing and implementing vendor governance, qualification, oversight, performance management, and risk-management frameworks.
  • Strong knowledge of clinical trial operations, vendor service delivery models, Good Clinical Practice (GCP), International Council for Harmonisation (ICH) guidelines, and applicable regulatory requirements.
  • Experience with vendor contracting, financial oversight, spend analysis, sourcing strategy, and performance metrics.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead complex, cross-functional initiatives and influence stakeholders at all levels of the organization and with external partners.
  • Strong leadership, negotiation, facilitation, communication, and relationship-management skills.
  • Excellent analytical, strategic-thinking, decision-making, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to anticipate risks and develop practical mitigation plans.
  • Very organized and detail-oriented, with effective planning and time-management skills and demonstrated agility in prioritizing multiple competing demands in a fast-paced environment.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office 365; experience with vendor-management, procurement, quality, or reporting systems is an asset.
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills in English; French is an asset.

Our company

At Indero, you will work with brilliant and driven colleagues. Our values are collaboration, innovation, reliability and responsiveness. We offer a stimulating work environment and attractive advancement opportunities.

In this position, you will be eligible for the following perks:

  • Permanent full-time position
  • Flexible schedule
  • Vacation
  • Home-based position
  • Ongoing learning and development

A Global Clinical Leader In Dermatology!

﻿Formerly known as Innovaderm, Indero is a world-renowned expert and clinical research leader in dermatology. We have more than two decades of experience serving a broad range of indications, patient populations, administration routes, and drug classes, and a global footprint.

﻿Indero is a dual-focus CRO for dermatology and rheumatology, with 25+ years’ experience in clinical research and trial delivery. Our full-service approach – which includes everything from protocol design and patient recruitment to trial monitoring and biometrics – provides biotech and pharmaceutical sponsors with the rigorous scientific foundation and tailored expertise their studies need to reach the finish line efficiently and effectively. Responsibilities

Peraton is seeking an experienced Software Quality Assurance Engineer to independently execute and take expanded ownership of quality assurance and test automation activities on the BASIS program. Operating with minimal supervision, the QA Engineer carries direct responsibility for automated test design and delivery, test documentation ownership, defect lifecycle management, and security testing integration — all in support of the program's automation-first QA mandate. All quality assurance activities must be automated.

The selected candidate will independently manage test automation deliverables across Agile sprint cycles, contribute to QA strategy discussions, support junior engineers, and interface with developers and Government stakeholders on quality metrics and release readiness across the deployment pipeline.

This is a 100% remote role.

Test Automation Development & Strategy

  • Independently design, develop, implement, and maintain automated test scripts for unit, integration, regression, and end-to-end functional testing across the application portfolio.
  • Ensure all automated test cases are executable by the end of each Agile sprint and fully integrated into the Government-managed DevSecOps pipeline with minimal oversight.
  • Drive and apply Test-Driven Development (TDD) methodology — authoring test cases prior to code development and collaborating closely with software engineers to align test coverage with functional requirements.
  • Lead the Test Automation State Assessment for assigned application areas; produce assessment reports with automation completion estimates.
  • Own the automation of adjacent legacy test cases per Government-approved schedules to systematically expand regression coverage across the portfolio.
  • Evaluate automation approaches and recommend improvements to test architecture, reusability, and pipeline integration within the Government-provided automation framework.
  • Serve as a technical resource and mentor to junior QA engineers on automation best practices, test script development, and tool usage.

Test Planning & Documentation

  • Develop and own Requirements Traceability Matrices (RTMs) at the end of each development cycle/sprint, ensuring full traceability and complete testing coverage of all functional and non-functional requirements.
  • Document all test activities, execution results, and defect findings within the Government-provided Test Case Management System with accuracy and completeness.
  • Independently prepare Testing Reports, Release Notes (Draft and Final), and Software Version Descriptions (SVDs) per release cadence requirements.

  • Enforce and monitor hard contractual quality thresholds with zero defects released to production.
  • Lead defect triage and root cause analysis in JIRA; manage the full escalation workflow to product teams with complete documentation and submit JIRA tickets prior to all escalations.

Our people are the backbone of everything we do and are our most valuable asset. Our business model demands top talent across the board, and we aim to create conditions that attract and retain the best individuals globally.

﻿Role Overview

We are expanding our Product team, and this role owns a slice of the internal product ecosystem our teams run the business on.

Your starting focus is the Media Buyer Automation Platform — the rules engine, pacing logic, spend controls, alerting, and workflow tooling that let a small team of buyers manage budgets that would otherwise require significantly more headcount. From there, your scope extends across the internal tools that support the wider acquisition engine: marketing automation, reporting and analytics workflows, creative operations, and the new tooling we build as the business shifts. We expect the exact portfolio to evolve, and we are hiring someone who wants that rather than someone looking for a single fixed product.

This is a hands-on builder role rather than a coordination role. Your users are colleagues, the feedback loop is short, and your work shows up in CPA, ROAS, wasted spend, and hours returned to the team. You will report to the Head of Product and work daily with Engineering, Data, Media Buying, Creative, and Operations.

Responsibilities

﻿

﻿1. Product Strategy & Roadmap

  • Own the end-to-end roadmap for the Media Buyer Automation Platform, including discovery, prioritization, specifications, delivery, adoption, and iteration.
  • Take on additional internal products as the portfolio grows, sequencing work across marketing automation, reporting and analytics, creative operations, cross-platform account management, and data reconciliation while maintaining focus on the core platform.

2. User Needs & Automation

  • Work closely with media buyers to understand their workflows and translate their operational needs into reliable automation for budget pacing, anomaly alerts, spend guardrails, bulk actions, and approval flows.
  • Identify manual processes that are consuming capacity across the business and evaluate whether they should be automated through internal development, external solutions, or left unchanged.

3. Product Development & Delivery

  • Write clear product specifications that engineers can build from, including edge cases, failure modes, rollback behavior, and a defined bar for completion.
  • Prototype ideas and build lightweight automations where this can accelerate alignment or address smaller workflow needs without relying on the engineering roadmap.

4. Adoption, Measurement & Collaboration

  • Drive product adoption through onboarding, enablement, documentation, and continuous feedback loops that ensure tools remain actively used and valuable.
  • Define and track meaningful product metrics, ensuring they are properly instrumented and visible, while partnering with Data on event taxonomy, attribution challenges, and measurement trade-offs.

5. Experimentation & Optimization

  • Run experiments and staged rollouts to validate changes, particularly for functionality that affects advertising spend, before deploying them across full budgets.
  • Continuously evaluate and iterate on products based on performance data, user feedback, and evolving business needs.

  • 4+ years in Product Management, with 2+ years owning data-heavy or workflow-heavy products end-to-end.

  • Skilled in KPI design, event taxonomy, dashboarding, and turning numbers into decisions.
  • Active use of AI tools (Cursor, Claude Code, Lovable, n8n, custom scripts) to build prototypes and automate workflows. (Examples will be requested).

  • Design and build distributed data pipelines (Apache Beam, Python) for large-scale document and model processing;

    Architect and build graph-based Knowledge Bases (Dgraph or similar), including schema design and query optimization;

  • Optimize LLM usage for cost, latency, and reliability in production environments;
  • Design and implement backend service layers (Go-based APIs) connecting AI pipelines with agent systems;
  • Ensure observability, debugging, and performance monitoring across distributed AI systems;
  • Package and deploy systems using Docker (docker-compose, containerized environments);

jobs.description:
At HVAC RNTL, we move fast—delivering commercial HVAC rental solutions when and where they’re needed most. From one-ton spot coolers to large-scale chillers and cooling towers, our team responds with speed and precision, whether it’s a planned project or a 24/7 emergency.

If you’re wired for problem-solving and thrive in a fast-paced environment, you’ll fit right in. Our people set us apart—and with locations across the U.S., there’s room to grow, take on big challenges, and make an immediate impact.

Applied Solutions Sales Manager

Remote / Travel / HQ Irving, TX

At HVAC RNTL, we're looking for an experienced HVAC sales manager who loves developing people, solving technical problems, working with customers, and growing a business.

This isn't a role where you'll spend your days managing people through reports and dashboards.

We want someone who wants to get into the field.

You'll travel with your sales team, walk jobs, meet customers, help think through complex temporary HVAC applications, develop territories, coach people, and help us decide where we should invest and grow next.

And you'll need to know HVAC.

Our Applied customers rely on us for more than equipment. They expect us to understand their systems, ask the right questions, anticipate challenges, and bring together the right equipment, people, and expertise to develop a solution that works.

You don't need to personally engineer every project or have every answer. But you should be comfortable talking about chillers, boilers, air handlers, pumps, airflow, water flow, temperature, pressure, power, controls, temporary distribution, and how these pieces interact in a temporary HVAC application.

If you've spent your career around commercial HVAC, that should feel natural.

What You'll Be Doing

Build and Develop a Great Sales Team

  • Lead and develop a geographically dispersed team of Applied HVAC sales professionals.
  • Spend significant time in the field coaching through customer visits, ride-alongs, job walks, and opportunity planning.
  • Recruit great people and help them build successful careers here.
  • Set clear expectations and hold people accountable.
  • Coach people who are struggling and help high performers continue growing.
  • Make the difficult people decisions that come with being a manager when necessary.
  • Identify and develop the next generation of leaders.
  • Build a team where people share knowledge, support one another, and enjoy winning together.

Help Your Team Solve Technical HVAC Problems

  • Work alongside representatives on complex temporary heating and cooling applications.
  • Help the team understand the customer's complete system and the problem we're trying to solve.
  • Ask the questions that help us get scope right before equipment arrives onsite.
  • Recognize when additional technical, operational, engineering, or safety resources need to be involved.
  • Help continually raise the technical capability of the sales organization.

Grow the Business

  • Own revenue growth and commercial performance across your markets.
  • Establish budgets, forecasts, territory plans, and growth expectations.
  • Help representatives develop their territories and customer relationships.
  • Identify new geographies, verticals, customers, and applications where HVAC RNTL can win.
  • Support major projects and strategic opportunities.
  • Help leadership understand where fleet and resources should be invested based on what you're seeing in the market.

Stay Close to Customers

  • Build relationships with contractors, engineers, facility leaders, end users, and strategic partners.
  • Be in front of customers with your team.
  • Help navigate technically complex projects and difficult customer situations.
  • Encourage the team to solve the customer's problem rather than simply rent them a piece of equipment.
  • Make it easy for customers to do business with us.

How We Lead

Our four Core Values are central to what we're building.

Prioritize People Know your team. Invest in them. Coach them. Challenge them. Help them grow. Hold people accountable while remembering there is always a person behind the number.

Own the Customer Experience Don't pass problems around. Take ownership, bring the right people together, communicate, follow through, and make it right.

Build Better Together Applied HVAC is a team sport. Sales, Operations, Service, technical resources, vendors, and customers all bring something to the table. We expect our leaders to collaborate, share expertise, and make the whole team better.

Deliver Results Move with urgency. Make decisions. Close loops. Keep commitments. Find solutions and get things done.

What We're Looking For

We're looking for someone who has actually lived in the HVAC world.

You should bring strong commercial HVAC knowledge along with a proven history of leading people. Ideally, you've worked in HVAC rental, applied equipment, mechanical contracting, commercial service, or another technical HVAC environment.

You should also have experience doing the real work of management—hiring people, developing them, promoting strong performers, addressing poor performance, making difficult personnel decisions, setting budgets, forecasting the business, and being accountable for your team's results.

Just as importantly, we're looking for someone who is professional, collaborative, curious, technically credible, comfortable with customers, and genuinely enjoys helping other people succeed.

Why HVAC RNTL?

We're not trying to become another big-box rental company.

We're building a focused HVAC organization where talented people have the ability to think, make decisions, solve problems, and take care of customers.

We believe accountability matters. Results matter. Technical excellence matters.

But people matter too.

We want our managers spending time with customers and sales teams—coaching, teaching, solving problems, developing markets, and building relationships—not creating activity simply so another KPI can turn green.

We're part of the broader Meriton ecosystem, giving our teams access to capabilities and relationships beyond rental while still allowing us to operate with the speed, ownership, and entrepreneurial mindset our customers value.

If you're an experienced HVAC sales manager who misses being close to customers, enjoys developing people, understands the technical side of the business, and wants an opportunity to help build something—we'd like to talk with you.

About the Role

We are looking for a Senior Data Center Solutions Engineer to work alongside our Sales teams and customers in developing complete, integrated data centre infrastructure solutions.

(Senior) AI Platform Engineer (m/f/d)

We are looking for an experienced (Senior) AI Platform Engineer (m/f/d) to design, run and keep improving modern, scalable AI and ML platforms. You will work with Kubernetes, GPU infrastructure, automation and Infrastructure-as-Code, along with modern CI/CD and MLOps processes, both on-premises and in the cloud. If you want to bring your expertise to innovative projects, we look forward to your application!

Who We Are

evoila is an European leader specializing in Cloud Infrastructure, Cloud Native, Data & AI, and App Modernisation, with a strong growth in Spain. We collaborate with medium and large enterprises to design and build modern, scalable, and secure cloud infrastructures.

We are recognized partners of VMware, Microsoft, and other industry leaders. Our approach? No fluff—just expertise and impact.

At evoila, exciting projects await you, where you will develop and implement innovative solutions for customers across various industries.

Your responsibilities

  • Plan, build and run highly available AI/ML platforms and services, mainly on Kubernetes, in on-premises, hybrid and cloud environments.
  • Design and implement scalable GPU infrastructure in Kubernetes clusters, including GPU scheduling and sharing (e.g. Kueue, KAI Scheduler, Run:ai, NVIDIA MIG/time-slicing), with a focus on utilization and cost efficiency.

  • Advise our customers on best practices, AI governance, data security and data protection for AI platforms on Kubernetes.
  • Work closely with data science, data platform and development teams so that AI solutions integrate smoothly.

What you bring

  • At least 3 years of experience running and optimizing platforms and services at scale in Kubernetes environments, on-premises or in the cloud.
  • In-depth knowledge of designing and running scalable Kubernetes-based solutions, ideally including GPU workloads.
  • Programming skills in Python, ideally also Golang or Java.
  • Experience with at least one model-serving framework (e.g. vLLM, NVIDIA Triton, KServe), and some or extensive experience with MLOps tools (e.g. MLflow, Kubeflow, ClearML).
  • Experience with Infrastructure-as-Code tools such as Ansible and Terraform, and with CI/CD and GitOps tools (e.g. Argo CD, Flux).
  • Excellent communication skills in Spanish and English. Ideally, you have advised customers before and can explain technical topics to any audience, from engineering teams to management.
  • NO remote position from other countries, candidates should be based in Spain.

Additionally for the senior role

  • 5+ years of relevant experience in platform engineering.
  • Architecture ownership: you are responsible for designing AI platforms end-to-end and make the core technology decisions.
  • Technical leadership in customer projects (lead role) and mentoring of colleagues.

Nice to have

  • Knowledge of running LLM-based architectures, e.g. RAG pipelines, vector databases and embedding services, as well as agentic AI approaches and the Model Context Protocol (MCP).
  • Understanding of the system-level basics of LLM serving (rate limiting, token streaming, load balancing) and of LLM concepts such as reasoning, tool calling and prompt templates.
  • Experience with new serving components such as llm-d or the Kubernetes Inference Gateway.
  • Knowledge of securing AI platforms, e.g. TLS, RBAC and network policies in Kubernetes environments, and a basic understanding of AI governance (e.g. the EU AI Act).
  • Certifications in relevant technologies (e.g. Certified Kubernetes Administrator/Developer, NVIDIA certifications).

Senior Finance Manager

Position Summary

The Senior Finance Manager is a strategic member of the Finance team responsible for financial planning and analysis, budgeting, accounting, federal grant financial management, compliance, and executive financial reporting for the Epilepsy Foundation of America. Reporting to the Chief Financial Officer and Treasurer, this position partners closely with executive leadership and department leaders to support informed decision-making, strengthen organizational financial performance, and ensure compliance with Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP), federal regulations, nonprofit accounting standards, and organizational policies.

This role requires an experienced nonprofit finance professional with expertise in financial planning and analysis, fund accounting, federal grant administration, budgeting, forecasting, and executive reporting. The ideal candidate possesses advanced proficiency in Sage Intacct, exceptional analytical skills, and the ability to translate complex financial information into meaningful insights that support organizational strategy.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

Financial Planning, Budgeting, and Analysis

  • Lead the organization's annual operating budget process and coordinate budget development across all departments.
  • Prepare annual budgets, quarterly forecasts, long-range financial projections, and financial models that support strategic planning and organizational decision-making.
  • Produce monthly budget-to-actual reports, including variance analyses, trend reporting, and actionable recommendations.
  • Develop financial dashboards, key performance indicators (KPIs), and executive reporting tools to monitor organizational performance.
  • Prepare financial reporting packages and presentations for executive leadership, the Finance Committee, and the Board of Directors.
  • Perform financial modeling, forecasting, scenario planning, and ad hoc analyses to support strategic initiatives.

Accounting and Financial Management

  • Support the monthly, quarterly, and annual financial close process, including journal entries, reconciliations, and financial statement preparation.
  • Ensure compliance with GAAP, nonprofit accounting standards, and internal financial policies.
  • Oversee the billing and revenue recognition function, including supervision of one direct report.
  • Monitor restricted and unrestricted net assets and ensure proper accounting for donor-imposed restrictions.
  • Manage revenue recognition for grants, contributions, contracts, bequests, investment activity, and special events.
  • Reconcile investment activity and prepare related journal entries.
  • Maintain effective internal controls while identifying opportunities to improve financial processes, reporting accuracy, and operational efficiency.

Federal Grants and Compliance

  • Manage the financial administration of federal grants, cooperative agreements, and government contracts throughout the grant lifecycle.
  • Prepare grant drawdown documentation for management review and approval.
  • Prepare and submit required federal financial reports, including SF-425 reports and other sponsor reporting requirements.
  • Monitor grant budgets, allowable costs, indirect cost recovery, carryforward balances, and budget modifications.
  • Prepare annual Incurred Cost Submissions (ICS), indirect cost calculations, and supporting schedules.
  • Coordinate grant closeouts, subrecipient monitoring, and ongoing compliance activities.
  • Ensure compliance with Uniform Guidance (2 CFR Part 200), sponsor requirements, and organizational policies.
  • Prepare supporting documentation for Single Audits, external audits, and other grant compliance reviews.

Leadership and Collaboration

  • Serve as a trusted financial advisor to executive leadership and department managers.
  • Partner with Finance, Development, Programs, Human Resources, and Operations to support organizational priorities and strategic initiatives.

Complex integrations are delivered cleanly, consistently, and fast. Our teams thrive in high-stakes environments where quality control and uptime matters, schedules are compressed, and coordination is everything.

Join us and be part of a team where your voice matters, your work makes an impact, and your growth is a shared priority.

Position Title: Engineering Manager - Design

Position Location: Remote - work virtually from anywhere in the United States

JOB SUMMARY

The Engineering Manager - Design provides leadership, expertise, and delegates work for design document deliverables for building automation system (BAS), electrical power monitoring system (EPMS), and software integration design projects in hyperscale data center and similar mission critical / technology sectors. This role leads a team of BAS / EPMS engineers, ensuring consistent delivery and quality across multiple MEP design programs by integrating lessons learned and leading the QAQC effort.

This position will work with internal and external MEP/FP trade engineers, equipment representatives, product vendors, and BIM / Revit / AutoCAD production resources.

The Engineering Manager – Design will be self-directed on day-to-day work and receive high level instruction on new projects, tasks or assignments. Will execute and lead teams and projects, tasks or assignments of complex scope. This role also will coordinate activities of other personnel and serve as a people manager.

This person will communicate and operate in line with organizational goals / values, and departmental objectives.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS

Develop and Execute Building Automation Systems Engineering Solutions (25%)

  • Serve as client program lead, project trade lead, and SME for the BAS and EPMS scope for one or more projects and / or programs.
  • Develop client standards, basis of design (BOD), perform feasibility studies, and assist clients with building automation roadmaps
  • Lead designs for DDC and PLC based BAS and EPMS systems
  • Design controls network / system architecture including IT / OT requirements
  • Select instrumentation, sensors, actuators, valves and other field devices
  • Coordinate with equipment, system, and product vendors for building automation interface requirements
  • Create and review project book and sheet specifications
  • Create and review sequence of operations
  • Create and review system diagrams and point / alarm lists
  • Work closely with client IT departments for network design, interface details, and security requirements
  • Provide direction on engineering production aspects with internal and external Revit / BIM resources

Training / Technical Firm Standards Development / Improvement of Policies and Procedures (30%)

  • Develop, maintain, and enforce organizational design standards, templates, and best practices for BAS / EPMS design projects alongside leadership
  • Mentor and train staff on technical competencies, software tools, and project workflows
  • Promote continuous improvement through lessons learned sessions on completed projects
  • Perform QAQC reviews for all project milestones on projects / programs where they are not lead engineer

Construction Related Process, Deliverables and Submissions (15%)

  • Accountable for design document deliverables for design phases including Schematic Design (SD), Design Development (DD), Issue For Permit (IFP), Issue For Construction (IFC)
  • Lead planning and execution of Construction Administration (CA) phase activities remote and on site
  • Lead building automation focused design reviews and page turns

Reporting and Communication (15%)

  • Prepare project progress reports for internal and external stakeholders
  • Manage personal hours using company tools

People Manager (15%)

  • Implement and monitor team objectives to meet set goals.
  • Manage and execute departmental or organizational projects, ensuring alignment with departmental focus.
  • Ensure employee adherence to company policies and procedures, serve as the first stop for employee questions on workplace rules and practices.

  • Participate in organizational strategy discussions to synchronize departmental and company goals.
  • Foster interdepartmental communication to enhance organizational understanding.
  • Align team efforts with overarching company strategies.
  • Communicate details effectively to all stakeholders.
  • Optimize resource management and task assignments within the team.
  • Adapt resource allocation in response to project demands and departmental needs.
  • Cultivate a team environment that encourages cooperation and collective problem-solving.
  • Assist with team and departmental hiring and recruiting processes.

Completion of Assigned Tasks and Deliverables on Time and on Budget

Performs Other Related Duties as Assigned

POSITION REQUIREMENTS (ADVANCED LEVEL FOR ALL THE FOLLOWING)

  • Skilled in navigating clients through BAS project designs including identification of standards, needs, and option evaluation
  • Skilled in completing assignments accurately and with attention to detail
  • Skilled at using MS Office Suite (Excel, Word, Outlook, PowerPoint, Teams), along with exceptional organizational skills for file management
  • Skilled in designing BAS and EPMS packages for MEP firm(s)
  • Knowledge of construction design process, stakeholders, deliverables
  • Knowledge of code requirements and energy guidelines related to BAS designs
  • Knowledge of data center HVAC applications and BAS control strategies including chilled water plants
  • Knowledge of IoT and smart building solutions
  • Knowledge of Networking including Addressing, VLANs, LANs, Switches and Routers
  • Knowledge of open-source protocols (BACnet, Modbus and SNMP)
  • Knowledge of DDC systems used in building automation designs
  • Knowledge of PLC systems used in building automation designs
  • Organizational skills, with the ability to manage multiple tasks simultaneously
  • Ability to leverage AI and emerging technologies to streamline workflows, optimize operational processes, and contribute to company-wide innovation
  • Ability to work successfully in a remote environment through effective communication and organizational skills, self-motivation, proactiveness and resourcefulness in a distraction free workspace
  • Ability to follow company and site safety requirements
  • Ability to analyze and prepare documents, reports and correspondence
  • Ability to communicate effectively in both oral and written form (technical and non-technical information)
  • Ability to communicate effectively directly with clients and at times serve as primary point of client contact
  • Ability to work successfully as a member of a team and independently with moderate supervision

PHYSICAL DEMANDS

EDUCATION / EXPERIENCE REQUIREMENTS

About us

Coalition is the world's first Active Insurance provider designed to help prevent digital risk before it strikes. Founded in 2017, Coalition combines comprehensive insurance coverage and innovative cybersecurity tools to help businesses manage and mitigate potential cyberattacks.

Opportunities to make an impact with bold thinking are real—and happening daily at Coalition.

About the role

We are looking for a Senior Software Engineer to provide technical leadership on Coalition’s Scanning Engine & Data Collection team. This team is responsible for the distributed systems that continuously scan the internet and our customers’ environments to collect the security data that powers our cyber insurance underwriting and our attack surface management product, Coalition Control.

In this role, you will design, build, and operate large-scale cloud services that run internet-wide and customer-specific scans, ingest and normalize third-party threat intelligence, and surface high-quality findings into our underwriting, risk, and security workflows. You’ll work closely with other senior engineers, security, product, and data teams to evolve the architecture of our scanning platform, improve its performance and reliability, and help mentor engineers across a distributed team spanning the US, Canada, and EU.

Responsibilities

  • Own end-to-end systems design for key components of the scanning engine, from initial design through implementation, deployment, and ongoing iteration
  • Design and implement high-quality services in Python and Go that power our scanning workflows, ensuring code is maintainable, well-tested, and observable.
  • Improve performance, scalability, and reliability of the scanning engine, optimizing for large-scale, distributed scanning workloads and strict SLAs.
  • Partner with security, product, and data teams to translate detection and scanning requirements into robust, production-ready systems and APIs.
  • Drive technical excellence and standards in the scanning engine codebase, including code review rigor, design documentation, and best practices for secure coding.
  • Contribute to architecture and roadmap decisions for the scanning platform, evaluating tradeoffs and proposing solutions that balance speed, quality, and risk.

  • Mentor and support other engineers on the team through design feedback, pairing, and knowledge sharing around systems design and scanning domain concepts.

  • Comfort operating in a fast-paced, evolving environment, making pragmatic technical decisions while maintaining quality and security.
  • Experience with code quality practices (testing, static analysis, code reviews) and building maintainable systems.

Bonus Points

jobs.excerpt: SS&C is a leading provider of mission-critical, AI-powered technology and services empowering financial services and healthcare organizations to work smarter, faster, and securely.
jobs.description:
SS&C is a leading provider of mission-critical, AI-powered technology and services empowering financial services and healthcare organizations to work smarter, faster, and securely. Founded in 1986, SS&C is headquartered in Windsor, Connecticut, and has offices worldwide. More than 23,000 financial services and healthcare organizations, from the world's largest companies to small and mid-market firms, rely on SS&C for expertise, scale, and technology.


Job Description


Senior Data Platform Engineer

Role Summary

We are seeking a Senior Data Platform Engineer to help build, scale, and operate our bespoke enterprise data platform, the foundational infrastructure layer that ingestion, ontology, and business application teams build on top of. This is a hands-on, individual-contributor role for someone who wants deep technical ownership of platform internals rather than owning specific business data pipelines: our platform stack spans Airflow, Iceberg, Spark, Flink, Kafka, Nessie, Trino, and StarRocks, along with supporting UI components for platform users.

You will not own the business logic of individual data pipelines; those are owned by application and business teams. Instead, you will build and harden the core platform capabilities that make those pipelines possible: ingestion frameworks, data cleansing/harmonization utilities, storage and compute infrastructure, and the APIs and agentic (MCP) interfaces that let both humans and AI agents access and operate on platform data and capabilities. You'll also be expected to bring an agentic software development approach to your own work, using AI coding agents and tooling to meaningfully multiply your engineering throughput, not just as an experiment on the side.

Key Responsibilities

Platform Capability Engineering

  • Design, build, and operate core platform capabilities on top of Airflow, Spark, and Flink for batch and streaming data processing, providing reusable frameworks that application/business teams use to build their own pipelines rather than building pipelines on their behalf.
  • Own the data lakehouse layer built on Iceberg, Nessie (catalog/versioning), Trino, and StarRocks, including table format management, catalog governance, query performance, and storage lifecycle (compaction, partitioning, retention).
  • Build and maintain Kafka-based streaming infrastructure (topics, schema management, connectors) that supports both platform-internal needs and consumption by downstream teams.
  • Develop reusable ingestion, cleansing, and harmonization frameworks/libraries that application teams can adopt to bring data onto the platform in a consistent, quality-controlled way, without the platform team owning each pipeline's business logic.
  • Build and maintain UI components that give platform users (engineers, analysts, business teams) visibility into platform state, data catalogs, job status, and data quality.

API & Agentic (MCP) Enablement

  • Design and build APIs that expose platform data and capabilities (ingestion, querying, catalog metadata, job orchestration) to downstream teams and services in a well-governed, secure, and performant way.
  • Build and maintain MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers/interfaces that expose platform data, catalogs, and lineage to AI agents and LLM-based tools, enabling agentic consumption of platform capabilities.
  • Extend agentic enablement beyond data access by building the tooling and guardrails that allow AI agents to safely operate parts of the platform itself (e.g., triggering pipeline runs, querying job status, remediation actions), with appropriate human-in-the-loop controls where needed.
  • Partner with platform consumers (including the Ontology Platform team) to understand their API/agentic access needs and translate them into platform capability requirements.

Scalability & Resilience

  • Ensure the platform scales reliably as data volume, source count, and consumer count grow, through capacity planning, performance tuning, and architectural evolution across the stack.
  • Design for resilience: fault tolerance, disaster recovery, data consistency guarantees, and graceful degradation across ingestion, storage, and compute layers.
  • Build and maintain observability (metrics, logging, tracing, alerting) across the platform stack to detect and diagnose issues before they impact downstream teams.
  • Drive on-call/production support practices for the platform, including runbooks and incident response processes.

Engineering Practice & Productivity

  • Adopt and champion an agentic SDLC approach, using AI coding agents and related tooling as a core part of your own development workflow to substantially multiply engineering throughput (targeting materially higher output than traditional development approaches, not incremental gains).
  • Establish and evolve engineering best practices for the platform team: testing strategy, CI/CD, infrastructure-as-code, and code/architecture review standards suited to a bespoke, multi-technology data platform.
  • Mentor other engineers on platform internals and on effective use of agentic development tooling, even without formal management responsibility.

Required Qualifications

  • 8-12 years of software/data engineering experience, with significant hands-on experience building or operating large-scale data platform infrastructure (not primarily building individual application-level data pipelines).
  • Deep, hands-on experience with at least several of: Apache Airflow, Apache Iceberg, Apache Spark, Apache Flink, Apache Kafka, Nessie, Trino, StarRocks, with the ability to reason confidently about the rest and ramp up quickly where needed.
  • Strong understanding of lakehouse architecture: table formats, catalog management, query engines, and the trade-offs between batch and streaming processing.
  • Experience designing and building APIs for platform capabilities, with an understanding of API governance, versioning, and security for multi-tenant platform consumers.
  • Direct experience with, or strong interest and rapid aptitude for, building MCP servers or similar agent-facing interfaces that expose data/capabilities to AI agents and LLM-based tooling.
  • Practical, hands-on experience using AI coding agents (e.g., Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, or similar) as a core part of your development workflow, with a track record of using them to meaningfully increase delivery speed and quality, not just occasional use.
  • Strong systems engineering fundamentals: distributed systems, performance tuning, capacity planning, and building for fault tolerance and resilience at scale.
  • Experience building and maintaining production observability (metrics, logging, tracing) for complex, multi-service data infrastructure.
  • Comfortable operating as an individual contributor with deep technical ownership, while also being able to mentor others and influence engineering practice without formal authority.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience building internal developer platforms or "paved road" tooling that other engineering teams adopt as self-service infrastructure.
  • Experience building agent-facing tooling or infrastructure beyond MCP (e.g., tool-use frameworks, agent orchestration, guardrails for autonomous agent actions).
  • Familiarity with UI/front-end development sufficient to build or contribute to platform-facing dashboards and tooling (not a primary requirement, but a plus).
  • Experience in financial services or another regulated, data-intensive industry, given the auditability and data-quality expectations typical of the domain.
  • Contributions to open-source projects in the Airflow/Iceberg/Spark/Flink/Trino ecosystem.

Unless explicitly requested or approached by SS&C Technologies, Inc. or any of its affiliated companies, the company will not accept unsolicited resumes from headhunters, recruitment agencies, or fee-based recruitment services.

SS&C Technologies offers a comprehensive total rewards package designed to support your wellbeing, growth, and future. Our benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage; a 401(k) plan with company match; paid time off, holidays, and parental leave; and professional development reimbursement opportunity.

Applications will be accepted on an ongoing basis until the position is filled.

Professional Volunteering

Professional volunteering is skills-based service performed with the same reliability, accountability, and quality expected in a paid professional role. Volunteers are core contributors whose work directly supports our mission of global compassion, collaboration, and action. Expectations include consistent weekly availability, timely communication, ownership and follow-through on assigned work, participation in team meetings, and alignment with our values and processes.

About Solution Community

Solution Community is an international 501(c)(3) nonprofit pioneering a social platform built to turn compassion into action. With volunteers from over 80 countries and experience drawn from companies like Apple, Google, Meta, Netflix, and Microsoft, we connect nonprofits, businesses, philanthropists, and volunteers to solve real social problems.

Our Mission

To foster a global community of compassion, uniting individuals and organizations to solve the world's social problems.

Our Vision

A world where every person has the opportunity to thrive — united by collaboration, compassion, and action.

Summary of Role

As Head of Sales, you will build and lead Solution Community's earned-revenue engine. This is not a donor-fundraising role — you will create sustainable, fee-for-service income for the organization. Your primary mandate is to launch and scale our advisory offering, which connects businesses and nonprofits with our vetted network of expert volunteers, and to develop paid partnerships that fund our mission. You will own the strategy, build the pipeline, close the first deals yourself, and lead a team of five Senior Sales Managers as the function grows.

What Will You Do?

  • Own and execute Solution Community's earned-revenue strategy — advisory/consulting engagements, paid B2B partnerships, and sponsorship packages that deliver real value to the buyer.

  • Stand up our consulting network from zero: define the offer, pricing, and revenue-share model that pays the expert volunteer and funds the organization.

  • Build a repeatable outbound sales motion — cold outreach, discovery, proposal, and close — using lean, low-cost tools.

  • Recruit, lead, and mentor a team of five Senior Sales Managers; set targets, run the pipeline, and hold the team to measurable revenue outcomes.

  • Build and manage relationships with businesses, nonprofits, and partners who buy or fund our services.

  • Track pipeline, conversion, and booked revenue; report results and forecasts to leadership.

  • Partner with Legal and Finance to keep earned-revenue activity compliant with our nonprofit status.

Who Are We Looking For?

  • 8–10+ years in sales, business development, or partnerships, with a proven record of closing revenue and hitting targets.

  • Experience building a sales function or offering from scratch — not just running an existing playbook.

  • Strong at outbound: comfortable owning cold pipeline, not waiting on inbound or warm networks.

  • Skilled at leading and coaching a distributed team.

  • Excellent communication, negotiation, and deal-closing skills.

  • Comfortable operating lean — no big tooling budget, high resourcefulness.

  • Committed to our mission, reliable, and accountable.

What We Offer

  • Global collaboration with leaders and strategists from top global companies.

  • Meaningful impact on global causes and communities.

  • A vibrant, multicultural team spanning 80+ countries.

  • A supportive environment rooted in compassion, integrity, innovation, and collaboration.

  • Flexible work-life with full autonomy.

The Curation Team turns a broad, global learning marketplace into focused, effective learning experiences for EMEA customers, prospects, and publishers. As a Curation Specialist, you will pair strong marketplace knowledge with a consultative approach to recommend the right content, build curated programs, and help EMEA customers make progress toward their workforce development goals — while accounting for the region's language diversity, local compliance needs (including GDPR), and varied working cultures.

What You Will Do

  • Translate the learning goals of EMEA customers and prospects into high-quality course mappings, curated lists, learning paths, and other recommendations that make the OpenSesame marketplace easy to use.

  • Create reusable programs, resources, documentation, and best practices that let OpenSesame deliver curation value consistently across EMEA markets and at scale.
  • Share marketplace and learning-industry insights relevant to EMEA with internal teams, and contribute to customer-facing resources, webinars, or other thought-leadership efforts.
  • Manage a portfolio of EMEA publisher relationships: act as the primary point of contact, coordinate internal support, share constructive feedback, and identify opportunities to strengthen the publisher offering in the region.
  • Surface content gaps, quality issues, and opportunities that improve how EMEA customers discover and use learning content — including content localized for the region's languages and regulatory requirements.
  • Keep requests, project details, and stakeholder communication organized and current in the team's operating systems. Deliver clear updates and dependable follow-through in a fast-moving environment, across time zones spanning the EMEA region.
  • Contribute to cross-functional initiatives aligned to team and company priorities, including improvements to curation processes, product experiences, and go-to-market enablement for EMEA.
  • Overlap your working hours with core EMEA business hours to stay accessible to regional customers, publishers, and colleagues.
  • Travel as needed for department and full-team events, both within EMEA and, occasionally, to global company gatherings — typically less than 10% of your time.

Performance Objectives

Within 30 Days

  • Build a comprehensive understanding of the OpenSesame curation process and tools.
  • Identify the needs of EMEA customers and see where curation fits into their journey.

Within 60 Days

  • Establish yourself as the internal and external expert on OpenSesame's course offering for the EMEA region.
  • Perform course mappings for EMEA customers regularly and navigate the OpenSesame catalog skillfully on a daily basis.
  • Establish relationships with at least 5 publishers serving the region.

Within 90 Days

  • Complete curation projects on behalf of 50 unique EMEA customers, and establish relationships with at least 15 publishers serving the region.
  • Curate elearning course curricula confidently to support the launch and expansion of customer training initiatives across EMEA markets.

Within 120 Days

  • Complete curation requests consistently.
  • Serve as each publisher's primary point of contact within OpenSesame, and coordinate internal efforts to support and maintain strong, ongoing publisher relationships across the region.

Within 1 year

  • Build strong relationships with 10 or more EMEA publishers, and earn consistently positive feedback from customers and internal stakeholders.
  • Support EMEA customers at every stage of the course curation process, and create actionable project plans based on their unique business skills training goals.

Within 18 months

  • Become the go-to resource on the team for questions related to OpenSesame's business skills catalog in EMEA. Think strategically about curation, and identify opportunities to develop programs that help EMEA customers curate at scale.
  • Earn trust as an expert for both internal and external stakeholders across the region.

Within 2 years

  • Earn promotion to Senior Curation Specialist, EMEA, after building a reputation of excellence with regional publishers, customers, and OpenSesame teammates

SuccessFactors Learning expertise and implementation support (40%)

Transition planning and workstream coordination (25%)

Testing, migration validation, and launch readiness (20%)

Stakeholder communication and documentation (10%)

ABOUT RELENTLESS

Relentless is an organizing company focused on unlocking political power through relational organizing. Relational organizing is the simple, proven concept that people talking to their friends and family is more effective than strangers talking to strangers. Our flagship product, Rally, is a social graph, power-mapping tool, and program management platform that makes running scaled relational programs simple. Our in-house program team brings their deep experience to supercharge the programs that run on Rally and mobilize communities at scale to have meaningful conversations, get out the vote, and so much more.

This cycle, we’re running Rally Organizing programs that compensate tens of thousands of low-turnout voters for their time as they learn about upcoming elections and mobilize and persuade their friends and family to vote.

ABOUT THE ROLE
  • Program Organizers are at the heart of our Rally Organizing Programs — a high-energy, community-driven effort to activate voters and change their relationship to democracy. You'll help create virtual experiences that leave participants feeling enthusiastic, supported, and confident as trusted messengers in their communities.
  • This is a fast-paced, scaling program, and we're looking for someone who hits their stride in that kind of environment — someone who picks up new information quickly, adapts as priorities shift, and brings genuine passion for democratic participation to everything they do. Program Organizers develop a deep, holistic understanding of the program that allows them to move fluidly between shift types, carrying knowledge and momentum from one role into the next.

DETAILS & COMPENSATION

Type: Part-time, Hourly

Location: Remote

Pay: $25/hour

Reports To: Deputy Director of Programs, Organizer Experience

This is a part-time temporary cycle position with an anticipated start date of October 6, and end date of November 13, 2026. We are looking for a minimum availability of 15 hours per week within the hours of 11am- 10pm CT, Monday - Saturday, with a cap of 29 hours per week.

We will be reviewing applications on a rolling basis, and the bulk of the hiring for this role will take place in mid to late September.

JOB DUTIES

Event Leadership: Program Organizers lead our 1-hour virtual events end-to-end, serving as the face of the program to participants. Each event involves filling one of three rotating event roles, managing breakout rooms throughout the session, and monitoring rapid-response Slack channels in real time.

Above all, Program Organizers foster a positive, inclusive environment where participants feel supported, confident, and excited about the work they're doing. A customer service and solutions-oriented mindset is key — you'll be fielding questions on the fly and helping participants troubleshoot in real time, all while keeping the energy high.

Inbox Support: Program Organizers take scheduled shifts as the primary point of contact for our participants, responding to inquiries via the program inbox and providing timely, accurate, and helpful information. You'll assist participants in navigating program logistics, requirements, deadlines, and resources — and where needed, identify and troubleshoot issues or escalate them to the appropriate team.

This isn't just reactive support. You'll proactively follow up with participants to ensure they're on track, help with onboarding processes, and gather feedback on participant experiences to share with the broader team. A solutions-oriented mindset and genuine empathy for participants are essential — we want every participant to feel supported every step of the way.

Additional Duties: As our program grows and evolves, additional shifts and responsibilities may arise. Program Organizers are expected to step up where needed during their assigned shifts and adapt with the team.

Who We're Looking For

You're comfortable and energized by fast-paced environments. You're a strong, warm communicator, reliable with your assigned shifts, and a team player who actively shares information across roles. Experience with virtual event facilitation is a plus, and comfort with Slack and managing multiple channels is a must.

This position is entirely virtual and requires access to a computer, reliable internet, and a quiet place to host online events.

In lieu of a cover letter, we are asking you to answer the following questions below, which includes a short skills assessment and video recording. We will be hiring this role on a rolling basis and we commit to providing a monthly update on where we are in our process. The bulk of our hiring will take place in mid to late September.

jobs.description:
Overview
Ontrac Solutions is seeking a high-aptitude Production Engineer (IC2) to support a large-scale enterprise OS modernization and infrastructure hardening program for one of our enterprise clients. This role is built for an engineer with real software engineering foundations — specifically Python — who has since moved into infrastructure and is comfortable working across OS modernizations (RHEL7 → EL8/EL9), packaging migrations (Chef → CINC), and CI/CD hardening, while simultaneously executing hands-on runbooks, automation, and service onboarding.

This is a genuine hybrid role: roughly half build — Python tooling, RPM packaging, pipeline and rollback work — and half operate — runbooks, service onboarding, and Tier-2 break/fix. You will work directly with the client's SRE organization, internal engineering teams, and customer stakeholders from initial definition through final delivery. Candidates who are pure application developers with no Linux fleet exposure, and candidates who are pure operations with no real software engineering behind them, will not clear screening.

What your application must clearly show
We screen against the requirements below exactly as written — your resume should make these easy to find. Specifics matter more than vocabulary: a resume that restates this posting's terminology without the detail below will not advance.

  • Python you actually wrote, described as software, not as a skills keyword. Name the project, what it did, who depended on it, and how it was tested and shipped. "Python (scripting)" in a skills list will not clear this bar. A GitHub, GitLab, or public repo link is strongly preferred — we look at code.
  • RPM packaging you personally did. Name the .spec files you authored or maintained, how you handled dependencies and versioning, your build tooling (rpmbuild, mock, Koji, or an internal builder), roughly how many packages you owned, and where they were published.
  • A real OS migration you worked on — with version numbers and what actually broke. System Python 2→3, OpenSSL and crypto-policy changes, systemd unit differences, deprecated or renamed packages. We are more interested in the failure modes you hit than in the name of the program.
  • Configuration management you have run in production — Chef (cookbooks, recipes, Ohai, Test Kitchen/InSpec), CINC, Puppet, Ansible, or Salt. Say which resources you wrote and how you tested convergence.
  • Monitoring and logging work you executed. Name the stack, what you onboarded to it, and what you actually instrumented — metrics, dashboards, alert rules, log pipelines — not just the product name.
  • Tier-2 or on-call experience: the rotation you carried, the scale of the fleet behind it, and one incident you personally drove to resolution.
  • CI/CD pipelines you built or hardened, including how rollout and rollback were handled when a change went wrong.
  • Your certifications, named, with dates and credential IDs or verification links — we verify certifications.

Shortly after you apply you will receive a short role-specific questionnaire — completing it promptly is the fastest way to move into screening.

Required Qualifications:

  • Software engineering foundation: 3+ years of professional software engineering experience, with strong hands-on Python. You have written and maintained code other engineers depended on — modules, packaging, tests, code review, and version control, not just single-file scripts.
  • Enterprise OS modernization: Hands-on experience with enterprise Linux at fleet scale and with large-scale OS upgrade programs — RHEL7 → EL8/EL9 or an equivalent major-version migration you executed rather than observed.
  • Packaging migrations: Experience building RPM packages to replace legacy configuration, and with large-scale packaging or configuration-management migrations such as Chef → CINC.
  • Independent bug ownership: Able to triage, own, and resolve bugs end to end without hand-holding — reproduce, isolate, fix, test, and ship.
  • CI/CD and release safety: Ability to harden CI/CD pipelines, observability frameworks, and rollout/rollback mechanisms specifically tailored for legacy-to-modern infrastructure transitions.
  • Tier-2 operational support: Willingness and experience to partner closely with an SRE team providing "follow-the-sun" tier-2 support, including hands-on incident response and break/fix operations on existing platforms.
  • Service onboarding: Experience onboarding services to newly established monitoring and logging stacks.
  • Automation and documentation: A demonstrated habit of automating repetitive operations and documenting technical procedures for others to run.
  • Location and work authorization: Must be located in the United States and authorized to work in the US.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Proven experience planning and executing logging and monitoring tool rollouts end to end — not only operating a stack someone else stood up.
  • Experience supporting a team through cloud cutovers and component migrations to cloud environments.
  • Perl scripting experience — legacy tooling in this environment is Perl, and the ability to read and safely modify it is a real advantage.
  • Hands-on exposure to modern observability tooling — Chronosphere, Prometheus, or Grafana — and to Splunk integrations.
  • Provisioning and image work: Kickstart/PXE, golden images, or repository and mirror management.

Key Responsibilities — OS Modernization & Packaging:

  • Drive the technical transition of legacy systems to modern enterprise Linux environments, including RHEL7 → EL8/EL9 upgrade paths.
  • Build and maintain RPM packages to replace legacy configuration, and carry the packaging migration from Chef to CINC.
  • Develop and execute automated runbooks that make the migration repeatable rather than manual.
  • Triage, own, and resolve migration bugs independently, from first report through verified fix.

Key Responsibilities — Observability & Monitoring Transition:

  • Transition monitoring infrastructure to a modern stack — Chronosphere, Prometheus, and Grafana — and manage Splunk integrations.
  • Onboard services to the newly established monitoring and logging stacks, including metrics, dashboards, and alert rules.
  • Harden observability frameworks alongside the pipelines they instrument, so regressions surface before users find them.

Key Responsibilities — CI/CD, Rollout & Rollback:

  • Harden CI/CD pipelines for legacy-to-modern infrastructure transitions, including build, test, and package promotion stages.
  • Design and maintain rollout and rollback mechanisms that make large-fleet changes reversible.
  • Automate repetitive operational work and replace manual runbook steps with tested, reviewed code.

Key Responsibilities — Tier-2 Operations & Migration Support:

  • Provide Tier-2 operational support and incident response under a follow-the-sun model, in close partnership with the client's SRE team.
  • Perform hands-on break/fix operations on existing platforms while the modernization proceeds in parallel.
  • Assist application developers with architectural support and troubleshooting during cloud migration phases.
  • Author and maintain technical documentation — runbooks, migration procedures, and package and pipeline ownership notes.

Leitung Programm & Netzwerkarbeit (m/w/d)

Unbefristet | Vollzeit | Ab sofort | Remote (Deutschland)

Heimatwurzeln ist ein gemeinnütziger Verein mit einem besonderen Anspruch: Wir machen Umwelt- und Klimaschutz für Menschen aus der bürgerlichen Mitte – also für die, die sich oft nicht als Teil der Klimadebatte sehen. Dabei setzen wir auf Werte wie Heimatverbundenheit, Traditionen, Pragmatismus, Verantwortungsbewusstsein und gesunden Menschenverstand.

Strategische Programmverantwortung

Netzwerk, Partnerschaften und Finanzierung

Führung und Zusammenarbeit

Ihr Profil

  • Mindestens 7 Jahre einschlägige Berufserfahrung in relevanten Feldern (Verbandswesen, Public Affairs, Projektleitung, Verwaltung/Politik, Beratung o. Ä.) mit nachweislicher Erfahrung im Umgang mit hochrangigen Entscheidungsträgern

  • Sehr gutes Verständnis des politischen Umfelds in Deutschland, insbesondere der bürgerlich-konservativen Milieus

  • Ausgeprägte Kommunikationsfähigkeit und souveränes Auftreten: überzeugend und verbindlich auf Augenhöhe in politischen, zivilgesellschaftlichen und institutionellen Kontexten

  • Analytisches und vorausschauendes Denkvermögen, sehr gute Allgemeinbildung und ein professioneller Umgang mit unterschiedlichen Perspektiven – Sie erkennen Chancen, Risiken und Dynamiken frühzeitig

  • Hohes Maß an Eigenverantwortung sowie initiativem, vorausschauendem und verbindlichem Arbeiten mit Builder-Mindset

  • Teamplayer mit Freude an einem Mix aus Remote-Office, Vor-Ort-Projekten und bundesweiten Terminen mit Partnern und Stakeholdern

  • Sehr gute Deutsch- und Englischkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift

  • Bereitschaft zu regelmäßigen Dienstreisen

Was wir bieten

  • Mitarbeit an einem einzigartigen, gesellschaftlich relevanten Projekt mit viel Gestaltungsspielraum

  • Schlüsselrolle mit spürbarem Gestaltungs- und Aufbauauftrag

  • Ein realistischer, bodenständiger Zugang zum Thema Umwelt- und Klimaschutz
